correctness.rationale: For all m,n>=3 and 0<=t<=min(m,n), every vertex-cover complement is a one-shore subset or a single missing matched pair. Full edge-distance comparisons prove that a one-shore omitted set is resolving precisely when it contains no more than one unmatched vertex. Each mixed pair is resolving by distinct selected-endpoint intersections. Enumerating these exhaustive disjoint cases (with empty-set correction) yields H=(1+z)^t(2+(m+n-2t)z)-1+t z^2. Inclusion maximal omissions yield M and the exact minimum. All distances (1,2,3) are valid even at m=n=3. The BFS exact-subset program checked 71 cases with m+n<=11; independent pair-witness C++ checked 108 cases with m+n<=12. No finite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The directly motivating 2023 source gives only Ddim_e(K_mn)=m+n-1 (the t=0 endpoint). Matching-deleted graphs with t>0 are not graph joins and cannot be obtained from that source’s join formula. The other most similar results concern vertex resolving polynomials, edge metric dimension without a cover, or the distinct vertex-edge domination condition. Actual literature and published-record searches showed no exact H/M expression or implication of it; historical uniqueness remains provisional.

value.rationale: This is a complete, natural two-parameter matched-edge-deletion response law for a combined identification/coverage invariant, not a single routine decrement. It classifies all feasible and inclusion-minimal sensor sets, identifies exactly when and how the biclique result changes, and shows an unbounded separation between the two inclusion-minimal sizes as the matching length increases. It also treats the balanced full matching endpoint with a distinct dimension plateau. The exact H polynomial permits future reliability and optimization calculations without recomputing the graph-specific edge-distance constraints.
